roadmap_item.title: Simplify Cassor skills and measure orchestration efficiency
roadmap_item.description: Keep Cassor guidance lightweight for ordinary work, load runtime-specific delegation details on demand, and measure comparable workflow efficiency without persisting transcripts.
roadmap_item.rationale: The core delivery contract, bounded context, portability, and capability dossier are now established; the skill layer should minimize unnecessary context and make efficiency claims evidence-based.

goal: Cassor skills provide proportionate, runtime-neutral workflow guidance with on-demand delegation details and a reproducible efficiency benchmark that reports only observed metrics.

included: Runtime-neutral entry skill guidance for lifecycle, authority, approval, amendment, and completion gates
On-demand adaptive orchestration reference for capability detection and model routing
Removal of duplicated instructions across the entry skill, protocol, and skills specification
Lightweight guidance for small local changes without weakening CLI-enforced gates
Static skill/reference validation and installer coverage
Comparable benchmark scenarios for small fixes, features, amendments, and resumed tasks
Aggregate benchmark reporting outside canonical SQLite state
excluded: New runtime adapters or worker integrations
Changes to Cassor lifecycle authority or persisted workflow semantics
Persisting raw transcripts, hidden reasoning, or benchmark telemetry in SQLite
Claims about worker-model or token efficiency when the runtime does not expose those metrics

decisions: SKILL.md remains the concise entry point; detailed dispatch policy lives in references/adaptive-orchestration.md and is loaded only when delegation is useful.
The protocol remains the authority reference; repeated policy text is removed from other documents rather than weakening the approval and worker-safety rules.
The CLI remains the only authority for persisted transitions; lightweight guidance may omit proportionate artifacts but never approval, amendment, or verification gates.

Benchmark scenarios use fixed fixtures and comparable successful outcomes; elapsed time, calls, output size, and repair effort are recorded only when observed, while unavailable token or worker metrics remain explicitly unavailable.
Aggregate benchmark results are retained as a reviewed repository document under docs/spikes and never written to canonical Cassor state.

acceptance_criteria.title: Small local changes have a documented lightweight path that preserves execution readiness, amendment, and completion gates.
The entry skill does not require runtime-specific dispatch or model-routing details for every task; those details are available through an explicit reference.
The portable skill, protocol, specification, and installed assets consistently direct agents to the Cassor CLI for legal state transitions.
Four representative benchmark scenarios produce comparable successful outcomes and report observed efficiency metrics without fabricating unavailable telemetry or persisting raw transcripts.

constraints: Preserve the seven lifecycle phases as guidance.
Preserve centralized user interaction, explicit approval, bounded implementation authority, and independent verification boundaries.
Keep portable skill installation and embedded assets deterministic.
Do not add runtime-specific behavior that cannot be verified by the current Codex runtime.

tasks.title: Refactor the entry skill and add on-demand orchestration guidance
tasks.description: Reduce SKILL.md to runtime-neutral workflow guidance, add the adaptive-orchestration reference, and preserve the full capability fallback and worker-safety contract.

tasks.title: Simplify protocol documentation and validate proportionate paths
tasks.description: Remove duplicated instructions across the portable protocol and skills specification, document lightweight small-change handling, and add static checks for references, frontmatter, and CLI authority wording.

tasks.title: Build the representative efficiency benchmark
tasks.description: Create fixed benchmark scenarios for a small fix, feature, amendment, and resumed task; measure successful outcome, observed calls, elapsed time, output size, repair effort, and unavailable telemetry without persisting raw runs.

tasks.title: Verify installed assets and record benchmark findings
tasks.description: Exercise deterministic skill installation and stale-file protection, run the benchmark and full repository checks, update the skills specification and aggregate benchmark report, and confirm Cassor state remains valid.

risks: Removing duplicated text can accidentally hide an authority rule; static tests must require links to the canonical protocol and role contracts.
The current runtime does not expose safe worker isolation or token telemetry, so the benchmark must report those dimensions as unavailable rather than infer them.
Generated installed assets and documentation projections can drift unless the embedded installer tests and deterministic build checks are updated together.
